body.p: During in-progress operations, the Git Client informs the user of the current operation on Git Staging and visualises it in the revision graph on Git History. In-progress operations include merging, rebasing, cherry-picking, and reverting.
The Git Staging view identifies the operation type (for example, Merging...).

fig.title: Git Staging view during a merge conflict

body.p:
The Git History table displays an amber label next to the source commit. The label text describes the current operation: Source commit labels
Operation Label text What it identifies
Merge Incoming (Theirs) The merge source commit.
Cherry-pick Cherry-picked commit The cherry-picked commit
Revert Reverted commit The commit the branch will revert to.
During a merge or rebase conflict, the Git History view also shows an amber Start (Mine) label next to the current commit.
To help you visualise in-progress operations, the Git Client also draws a dashed grey line from the merge source to the current branch's Uncommitted changes node.

fig.title: Git History view during a merge conflict
